summary_paragraph: Mr. Meléndez, a man with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy, systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and chronic alcohol use, was admitted for hematemesis and abdominal pain. He reported vomiting several cups of blood and had a history of gastritis. Initial concerns for mesenteric ischemia due to rising lactate were ruled out by abdominal CTA, which showed patent vasculature. He was treated with IV pantoprazole, fluids, and symptom management. His condition stabilized, with no further bleeding, and he tolerated a gradual diet advancement. His heart medications, including metoprolol, losartan, and Pradaxa, were restarted. He expressed interest in alcohol rehabilitation, and plans were made for transfer to a facility post-discharge. He was discharged home with follow-up instructions and prescriptions.
problems: Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, with hemorrhage
